content.rendered: It never was, they’re banking on people being too lazy/not wanting to eat any fees to transfer their money out of USB to somewhere else. I reckon if even a tiny percentage of people behave in this manner USB has more than profited from this little charade.

It is unbelieveable they would kill the card outright so quickly without trying to salvage it. They spent a lot of time and energy promoting the launch of it, alongside all the complementary bank accounts. There are other ways to salvage it – put a cap on it like Alliant’s 2.5% card, lower the interest rate on the deposit accounts, require a mortgage for the highest tier, or even re-issue it as an Infinite card to command higher interchange and tack on an annual fee to cover the increased costs of those benefits.

Again though, like I said a few weeks back – US Bank was never a good fit for this card. They are too conservative and risk averse and we’re now seeing the result of that. I will say though that offering higher credit card rewards at the expense of lower interest is something that appeals to high income individuals – interest is taxed, rewards are not. I could see something like that working with a minimum deposit in a low-yield account.
